description.narrative: Brazil's universal health system (SUS) has improved health outcomes significantly, but access to primary care is still a challenge due to long wait times, service shortages, and uneven regional coverage. Dr.Consulta addresses these gaps by offering subscription-based, tech-enabled primary care to middle-income Brazilians without private insurance. The proposed equity investment will fund new clinics and strengthen IT systems, expanding access through its hub-and-spoke model. This growth will improve affordable care availability and enhance Brazil's healthcare competitiveness by scaling a key player and driving market efficiency.

Founded in 2011, Dr. Consulta Holding S.A. (DrC) is a Brazilian tech-enabled healthcare platform that provides affordable, out-of-pocket primary and secondary care through an integrated model combining diagnostics and telemedicine. With 30 clinics across São Paulo, DrC serves low- and middle-income populations who are underserved by the public system and excluded from traditional private care. DrC leverages a subscription-based model offering discounted services and family coverage.
IFC is proposing a preferred equity investment of up to USD 30 million to build clinics in the state of São Paulo as well as nationally across Brazil. The investment will also strengthen DrCs technology infrastructure, driving operational efficiency and enhancing patient engagement.
